title: Line Heights
slide_intent: Balance tight rhythm with legibility because different sizes and letter cases need different amounts of vertical room.
strategic_value: Consistent square setting can give Burger King copy a compact rhythm while the stated exceptions protect small text and uppercase headlines.
demonstration: Three numbered text blocks demonstrate 120/120, 72/72 and 36/36 settings; left copy explains the 1:1 default and exceptions.
practical_value: Start with leading equal to point size, then evaluate the two explicitly allowed exceptions.

ingredient.name: Square line-height setting
ingredient.role: Keep text blocks compact without losing readability.
ingredient.application: Set leading equal to point size by default. Below 12 pt, leading may increase, for example 10/12 pt; Flame Bold caps may reduce it, for example 204/168 pt.
ingredient.scope: Historical 2020 partner guidelines, PDF produced January 2021. The next page supplies a separate 75% rule for all-caps headlines; preserve both source statements rather than treating the example here as that ratio.

reference_purposes.Application: Three numbered specimens demonstrate square line-height settings.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The default is 1:1 point size to leading; below 12 pt leading may increase, and Flame Bold caps may use reduced leading.
